chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The funeral (of the deceased) is announced to the people.

key_terms.الْجِنَازَة: Funeral or the deceased's body prepared for burial

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on announcing a person's death and funeral?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from al-Kafi underscores the communal nature of death rites in Shia jurisprudence, where announcing the 'Jinazah' (funeral) serves as a social obligation to facilitate collective mourning and prayer. It reflects the early Islamic practice of public proclamation to ensure the community participates in honoring the deceased, a principle foundational to the etiquette of death (Adab al-Mawt).

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from one of his companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The funeral, the people would be proclaimed with it’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from certain persons of his people who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
people should be informed to attend the funeral of a deceased person.”
